newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH FIN MIN DISMISSES FEARS OF C/A SURPLUS FALL.
newsitem.headline: DANISH FIN MIN DISMISSES FEARS OF C/A SURPLUS FALL.

text.p: Danish finance minister Mogens Lykketoft on Monday dismissed analyst fears of a dramatically shrinking current account surplus for 1997.
"The latest figures give me no cause to adjust our earlier forecasts for the full year," Lykketoft told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"The fall in the current account surplus in the first half of the year will right itself. I do not believe that Danish domestic consumption is rising so strongly that it will upset our previous estimates," he said.
The latest Danish Economy Ministry forecast in May foresaw a current account surplus of 12.0 billion crowns for this year, but the ministry is due to release fresh forecasts later this month.

Last Wednesday the Danish Statistics Office released data showing that May's current account surplus was 0.3 billion crowns, compared to a balance in April and a 1.83 billion crown surplus in May 1996.
The data brought Denmark's current account surplus for the first five months of 1997 to a combined 3.6 billion crowns, against 13.0 billion crowns for the same 1996 period.
Analysts expressed concern about the falling Danish current account, some of them predicting that the surplus could fall to around five billion crowns compared to last year's 16.7 billion crowns.

Some recommended that the government consider taking action to brake domestic consumption, pointing to the housing market as an area where the government could move in to curb demand. --Erik Matzen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969651
